world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Words with more than one syllable usually have the stress on the penultimate syllable. If the root has only one syllable, and the word has a prefix, the stress is on the prefix. [ˈipox] ‘su barriga’ [ˈnowan] ‘with me’ [ˈipan] ‘above it’ There are some postfixes that are not counted, though, like the absolutive suffix –tli, locative suffix -co, plural suffix –ten, and –qui which makes verbs into nouns. When a word ends on these postfixes, the stress is on the antepenultimate syllable. [...] Words borrowed from Spanish that do not have penultimate accent in Spanish do carry penultimate accent in SMT Nahuatl, like [ˈdoktor] ‘doctor’ [ˈkahfen] ‘café’

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. When the root is monosyllabic and carries a prefix, the prefix (i.e. still the penult) is stressed. The suffixes -tli (absolutive), -co (locative), -ten (plural) and -qui (agentive nominalizer) are extrametrical: words ending in them are stressed on the antepenult (the penult of the stem without the suffix). Spanish loans are re-stressed to the penult. The p. 19 remark ('the penultimate syllable, which is regularly stressed in Náhuatl') confirms the default.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed (only a remark on p. 20 that a reduplicated vowel forms two syllable nuclei 'receiving two stresses').
new_statements.exceptions: Words ending in -tli, -co, -ten, -qui take antepenultimate stress (suffix not counted); the article 'in' never receives stress and is treated as an independent word (p. 25-26).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (prefix+root+suffix); isolated forms from a phonology sketch; no phrase-level data. Describes the San Miguel Tenango (Zacatlán) variety of nhi, not the Tlalitzlipa village itself.
new_statements.identity_note: tlal1234 is a Glottolog bookkeeping node for retired ISO code [nhj] 'Tlalitzlipa Nahuatl': one village near Zacatlán, Puebla, 108 speakers (1990 census) per Ethnologue 15; merged into [nhi] Zacatlán-Ahuacatlán-Tepetzintla Nahuatl (Glottolog zaca1241) by ISO change request 2006-101 (effective 2007-07-18) on the basis of mutual intelligibility reported by the SIL linguist (Petra Schroeder). No descriptive work on the Tlalitzlipa village variety exists in Glottolog, Crossref, OpenAlex or SIL's catalogue. The stress statement quoted is Schroeder 2015 on San Miguel Tenango (Zacatlán), i.e. the successor language zaca1241 [nhi], and should be credited to zaca1241, not to tlal1234.

new_statements.relation_note: No catalog record (in_catalog false). The two statements held by the project both read 'fixed: penultimate syllable'; existing_statement 1 is drawn from this very document (the English original SIL 61014 of which SIL 62739 is the translation), and existing_statement 2 (Schroeder 2014 Gramática, SIL 60590: 'El acento de una palabra cae en la penúltima sílaba') states the same placement. Nothing new is added beyond what statement 1 already records; the Spanish version, unseen, is by SIL's metadata a translation and is not expected to differ.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is regular on the penultimate syllable. Stated deviations: (a) with a monosyllabic root plus prefix the stress sits on the prefix (the examples given are disyllables, so still penultimate); (b) the author treats the absolutive -tli, locative -co, plural -ten and agentive -qui as 'not counted', giving antepenultimate stress in words ending in them (e.g. [ˈtilmahtɬiʔ] 'cloth', [tɬahˈpijalten] 'domestic animals'); (c) Spanish loans are re-stressed to the penult ([ˈdoktor], [ˈkahfen]); (d) the article 'in' is never stressed. Stress is presented as predictable, not contrastive; vowel length is contrastive and independent of stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described. Only remark: a reduplicated V.V / CV.CV sequence 'audibly consists of two syllable nucleuses, receiving two stresses', unlike a long vowel (printed p. 21, PDF p. 22).
new_statements.exceptions: Antepenultimate stress before the 'uncounted' suffixes -tli (absolutive), -co (locative), -ten (plural), -qui (deverbal noun); prefix stressed when the root is monosyllabic; Spanish loans adapted to penultimate stress; article 'in' never stressed; 'usually' hedges the main rule.
new_statements.identity_note: The document describes Nahuatl of San Miguel Tenango, Zacatlán, Puebla ('SMT Nahuatl') = ISO nhi, Glottolog zaca1241. Tlalitzlipa (tlal1234, a Glottolog bookkeeping node for retired ISO nhj, one village near Zacatlán, pop. 108 in 1990, merged into nhi in 2007 as a mutually intelligible dialect) is not named anywhere in the document; it is cited for tlal1234 only as the nearest first-hand description of the merged nhi language.

new_statements.quote: Los prefijos y los posfijos tienen un orden establecido, y otras palabras no pueden aparecer en medio de ellos. El acento de una palabra cae en la penúltima sílaba. [p. 27] ... En la mayoría de los casos esta sílaba no lleva acento, y entonces la i se introduce antes de la consonante, e.g. itkimpiya, inkowa, iktlalia. Sin embargo, si la sílaba que lleva el prefijo-consonante lleva acento se introduce la i después del consonante, e.g. kikwa, okipix, niyoj, tikaj. Compare las mismas radicales cuando la sílaba del prefijo-consonante lleva el acento y cuando no lo lleva (el acento siempre va en la penúltima sílaba): ikpixtok 'está teniendo' / okipix 'tuvo' [pp. 105-106]
new_statements.translation: Prefixes and postfixes have a fixed order, and other words cannot appear between them. The accent of a word falls on the penultimate syllable. ... In most cases this syllable does not carry the accent, and then the i is inserted before the consonant, e.g. itkimpiya, inkowa, iktlalia. However, if the syllable containing the consonant-prefix carries the accent, the i is inserted after the consonant, e.g. kikwa, okipix, niyoj, tikaj. Compare the same stems when the consonant-prefix syllable carries the accent and when it does not (the accent always goes on the penultimate syllable): ikpixtok 'is having' / okipix 'had'.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement (penultimate) as the existing statement from Schroeder 2015 Phonology of Nahuatl de San Miguel Tenango (SIL 61014). Adds only the interaction with prefix epenthesis (stressed n- surfaces as ni-, unstressed as in-). Like the phonology, it describes San Miguel Tenango (nhi/zaca1241), the language into which Tlalitzlipa [nhj] was merged, not the Tlalitzlipa village variety itself.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable; the position of the epenthetic i with single-consonant subject/object prefixes (iC- vs Ci-) depends on whether that prefix syllable is the (stressed) penult.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the grammar (it states the accent 'always' goes on the penult); the grammar is a morphosyntax sketch and does not repeat the phonology's remark about uncounted postfixes/clitics.
new_statements.identity_note: tlal1234 is a Glottolog bookkeeping node for retired ISO code nhj (Tlalitzlipa Nahuatl, one village near Zacatlán, Puebla), merged in 2007 into nhi Zacatlán-Ahuacatlán-Tepetzintla Nahuatl (zaca1241). Both listed works describe the San Miguel Tenango (municipio Zacatlán) variety of nhi; the word Tlalitzlipa does not occur in the grammar. No description specific to the Tlalitzlipa village exists among the sources found.
